When volatility drops below a threshold determined by fee rates and time to resolution, the fee term dominates, creating a 'sticky price' equilibrium where the market loses its ability to efficiently incorporate new information. This is formalized by setting Δp = 0, yielding a critical volatility-to-fee ratio σ* = λ / √τ. Above this threshold, prices are efficient; below it, they become inefficient due to frictional drag. The γ term captures the convex hedging costs that amplify price movements during periods of high activity, acting as a stabilizing feedback loop only when σ exceeds σ*.
